proposals.before: During the Wende reign he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai, then served as acting governor of Hua, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting Minister of Works.
proposals.after: During the Wende reign he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai, then served as acting governor of Hua, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting Minister of the Masses.
proposals.reason: 檢校司徒 is acting Situ (Minister of the Masses), not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: In the Wende era he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai Prefecture, then served as acting governor of Hua Prefecture, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting minister of works.
proposals.after: In the Wende era he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai Prefecture, then served as acting governor of Hua Prefecture, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting minister of the masses.
proposals.reason: Same 司徒 versus 司空 confusion in the literal rendering.

proposals.before: When Emperor Zhaozong came to Luoyang, Ding Hui was made Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court.
proposals.after: When Emperor Zhaozong came to Luoyang, Ding Hui was made a joint manager of government affairs.
proposals.reason: 同平章事 is the Tang chancellor formula, not an office of a Pacification Court.

proposals.before: In the fifth year the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, and Ding Hui was made chief campaign commander with the acting rank of Grand Mentor of State.
proposals.after: In the fifth year the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, and Ding Hui was made chief campaign commander with the acting rank of Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is acting Taiwei (Grand Commandant), not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: In the fifth year Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou; Hui was made chief campaign commander and acting grand mentor of state.
proposals.after: In the fifth year Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou; Hui was made chief campaign commander and acting grand commandant.
proposals.reason: Same Taiwei mistranslation in the literal field.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he died at Dayuan.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he died at Taiyuan.
proposals.reason: 大原 stands for Taiyuan; Dayuan is not the established English place-name, and the idiomatic already has Taiyuan.

proposals.before: After Zhuangzong took the throne, Ding Hui was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: After Zhuangzong took the throne, Ding Hui was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: 追贈太師 is a posthumous honorific grant, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Yan Bao, whose style name was Qiongmei, came from Yan Prefecture.
proposals.after: Yan Bao, whose style name was Qiongmei, came from Yun Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yun Prefecture, not Yan (兗).

proposals.before: Yan Bao, style name Qiongmei, was a native of Yan Prefecture.
proposals.after: Yan Bao, style name Qiongmei, was a native of Yun Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yun Prefecture; Yan Prefecture would be 兗.

proposals.before: In the eighth month Yan Bao surrendered Xingzhou. Zhuangzong praised him, raised him to acting Grand Mentor of State and Grand Councilor, and gave him titular command of Tianping and the southeastern campaign, treating him as an honored guest and ranking him above the other generals. On every major plan Zhuangzong consulted him and followed his counsel.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Yan Bao surrendered Xingzhou. Zhuangzong praised him, raised him to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor, and gave him titular command of Tianping and the southeastern campaign, treating him as an honored guest and ranking him above the other generals. On every major plan Zhuangzong consulted him and followed his counsel.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is acting Grand Commandant, not Grand Mentor of State (太傅).

proposals.before: In the eighth month Bao surrendered Xing Prefecture; Zhuangzong praised him, advanced him to acting grand mentor of state and Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court, made him titular military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner, treated him with guest ceremony, ranked him above the other generals, and whenever there was planning consulted and decided with him.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Bao surrendered Xing Prefecture; Zhuangzong praised him, advanced him to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor, made him titular military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner, treated him with guest ceremony, ranked him above the other generals, and whenever there was planning consulted and decided with him.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is not grand mentor; 同平章事 is not Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court.

proposals.before: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor;
proposals.after: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously granted the honor of Grand Preceptor;
proposals.reason: 追贈太師 is a posthumous honor, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor;
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously granted the honor of Grand Preceptor;
proposals.reason: 追贈 is posthumous bestowal of honor, not enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Fu Xi wept before Zhuangzong and said, "I am a man of Zhao. For generations my house served the Wang family. The late lord once gave me a sword and charged me to crush the murderers.
proposals.after: Fu Xi wept in the rain before Zhuangzong and said, "I am a man of Zhao. For generations my house served the Wang family. The late lord once gave me a sword and charged me to crush the murderers.
proposals.reason: Chinese 雨泣 states that Fu Xi wept in the rain; the idiomatic English drops 雨.

proposals.before: Huo Yanwei told him, "Of the ten men our lord trusts most, you are four of them—why still hesitate?"
proposals.after: Huo Yanwei told him, "Of the ten men our lord knows, you are the fourth—why still hesitate?"
proposals.reason: 公在其四 means Fu Xi ranked fourth among the ten men, not that he counted as four of them.

proposals.before: Huo Yanwei said to Xi: "Among the ten men the sovereign knows, you are four of them—why hesitate!"
proposals.after: Huo Yanwei said to Xi: "Among the ten men the sovereign knows, you are the fourth of them—why hesitate!"
proposals.reason: Literal 公在其四 is ordinal fourth, not a count of four men.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: 贈太師 is a posthumous honorific grant, not an enfeoffment (封).

proposals.before: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and ten children to lure him back, but he would not turn aside, and the siege pressed harder day by day.
proposals.after: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and children—ten persons in all—to lure him back, but he would not turn aside, and the siege pressed harder day by day.
proposals.reason: Chinese 母妻洎兒女十口 counts ten household members including mother and wife, not ten children besides them.

proposals.before: Mingzong suspended court for a day on hearing the news and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: Mingzong suspended court for a day on hearing the news and by edict posthumously honored him as Grand Tutor.
proposals.reason: 贈太傅 is a posthumous honorary office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Wang Zan was a son of the former Hedong military commissioner Wang Chongying.
proposals.after: Wang Zan was one of the sons of the former Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongying.
proposals.reason: 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong (河東); 諸子 marks him as one among several sons.

proposals.before: Wang Zan was a son among the sons of the former Hedong military commissioner Chongying.
proposals.after: Wang Zan was a son among the sons of the former Hezhong military commissioner Chongying.
proposals.reason: 河中 should be rendered Hezhong, not Hedong.

proposals.before: Early in the Tianfu era, after the Liang Founder pacified Hedong, he recalled the Wang family's old kindness and took Wang Zan into his staff.
proposals.after: Early in the Tianfu era, after the Liang Founder pacified Hezhong, he recalled the Wang family's old kindness and took Wang Zan into his staff.
proposals.reason: 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tianfu, after the Founder had pacified Hedong, recalling the Wang family's old favor, he recruited Zan as a guest aide.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tianfu, after the Founder had pacified Hezhong, recalling the Wang family's old favor, he recruited Zan as a guest aide.
proposals.reason: 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong.

proposals.before: Guo Chongtao sent envoys to reassure him. An edict made him deputy military commissioner of Xuanwu, in charge of the prefecture, with his acting rank of Grand Mentor unchanged.
proposals.after: Guo Chongtao sent envoys to reassure him. An edict made him deputy military commissioner of Xuanwu, in charge of the prefecture, with his acting rank of Grand Tutor unchanged.
proposals.reason: 檢校太傅 is Grand Tutor, matching 太傅 elsewhere in the chapter, not Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 贈 is a posthumous honorary office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 贈 is honorary posthumous appointment, not enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Yuan Xiangxian was the Liang Founder's nephew by marriage.
proposals.after: Yuan Xiangxian was the Liang Founder's nephew (his sister's son).
proposals.reason: 甥 here is the sister's son, a blood nephew, not a nephew by marriage.

proposals.before: Xiangxian was the Liang Founder's nephew by marriage.
proposals.after: Xiangxian was the Liang Founder's nephew (his sister's son).
proposals.reason: The Chinese 甥 marks descent through the Founder's sister, not a marital nephew.

proposals.before: He led troops against Zhuo County, failed to take it, and withdrew.
proposals.after: He led troops against Tiao County, failed to take it, and withdrew.
proposals.reason: 蓚縣 is Tiao/Xiu County (蓨), not Zhuo (涿).

proposals.before: He led troops to attack Zhuo County, did not take it, and returned.
proposals.after: He led troops to attack Tiao County, did not take it, and returned.
proposals.reason: 蓚縣 is Tiao/Xiu County, misread as Zhuo.

proposals.before: Before long he was transferred to Song and advanced to acting Grand Mentor of State.
proposals.after: Before long he was transferred to Song and advanced to acting Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant/Defender-in-chief, not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: Before long he was transferred to garrison Song Prefecture and advanced to acting grand mentor of state.
proposals.after: Before long he was transferred to garrison Song Prefecture and advanced to acting grand commandant.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太尉 was rendered as grand mentor of state, conflating 太尉 with 太傅.

proposals.before: His great-grandfather Jinchao was Vice Prefect of Chengdu; because of Xiangxian's eminence, the Liang court repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed him Left Vice Minister.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Jinchao was Vice Prefect of Chengdu; because of Xiangxian's eminence, the Liang court repeatedly posthumously honored him as Left Vice Minister.
proposals.reason: 贈 is a posthumous honorific promotion, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor. Under Later Zhou in the Guangshun era he was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and created Duke of Chu.
proposals.after: By patent he was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Preceptor. Under Later Zhou in the Guangshun era he was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.
proposals.reason: 冊贈太師 is a posthumous office grant, not an enfeoffment; 追封 applies only to the Duke of Chu.

proposals.before: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor of State.
proposals.after: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of Grand Mentor of State.
proposals.reason: 詔贈太尉 is a posthumous honorary office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Zhuangzong welcomed him, granted him the imperial surname and name Li, and formed his three thousand men and two officers into the Left and Right Support-the-Hegemon brigades under Shaowen and Cao Ru.
proposals.after: Zhuangzong welcomed him, granted him the imperial surname and personal name, and formed his three thousand men and two officers into the Left and Right Support-the-Hegemon brigades under Shaowen and Cao Ru.
proposals.reason: 賜姓名 grants surname and given name together; the English 'name Li' treats the imperial surname as the given name and omits Shaowen.

proposals.before: Wu Zhen showed no pity for his kin when they were tortured, and humanity was thin in him. He may have wished to follow Yue Yang's ruthless example, but that is no model for a worthy minister.
proposals.after: Wu Zhen showed no pity for his kin, and humanity was thin in him. Although he admired Yue Yang's example, how was that a fitting way to serve Marquis Wen.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 不憫其親 does not mention torture, and 豈事文侯之宜 names Marquis Wen rather than a generic worthy minister.

decisions.reason: The source office is 檢校司徒 (acting Situ). Minister of Works is 司空, so the original English misidentifies the honorific rank.
The literal field repeats the same 司徒/司空 error; acting minister of the masses matches 檢校司徒.
加同平章事 is the Tang formula for joint management of government affairs, not an office of a Pacification Court.
檢校太尉 is acting Taiwei (Grand Commandant). Grand Mentor corresponds to 太傅, so the original rank is wrong.
The literal rendering likewise turns 太尉 into grand mentor of state; grand commandant is the matching office.
卒於大原 uses 大 as a graphic variant of 太; the place is Taiyuan, already used in the idiomatic field, not a distinct Dayuan.
追贈太師 is a posthumous honorary grant. Enfeoffment would be 封; honored as Grand Preceptor is accurate.
鄆州 is Yun Prefecture. Yan Prefecture would be 兗州 (as in Zhu Jin's later loss of 兗), so the native-place name is a real error.
The literal field makes the same 鄆/兗 confusion; native of Yun Prefecture matches 鄆州人.
進位檢校太尉 is a promotion to acting Grand Commandant. The adjacent 檢校太傅 in s0029 shows the text distinguishes Taiwei from Taifu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 進位檢校太尉、同平章事

decisions.reason: The literal text misreads both 太尉 as grand mentor and 同平章事 as Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court; the replacement corrects both.
追贈太師 is posthumous bestowal of an honorary office, not a fief. The following 追封太原郡王 in s0053 shows the text itself distinguishes 贈 from 封.
The literal field repeats enfeoffed for 追贈; granted the honor of Grand Preceptor is the accurate verb.

decisions.after: Fu Xi wept bitterly before Zhuangzong and said, "I am a man of Zhao. For generations my house served the Wang family. The late lord once gave me a sword and charged me to crush the murderers.
decisions.reason: 雨泣 marks copious weeping (tears like rain). The original drops 雨, but the proposal's 'wept in the rain' invents weather that the surrounding units never state.
公在其四 is an ordinal: Fu Xi is the fourth of the ten men 主上所知. 'You are four of them' and 'trusts most' both distort the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 主上所知者十人，公在其四

decisions.reason: The literal 公在其四 must be 'the fourth of them', not a count of four men.
贈太師 is a posthumous honorary office. 封 would be required for an enfeoffment.
母妻洎兒女十口 counts ten household members in all, including mother and wife, not ten children besides them.
詔贈太傅 is an edict granting a posthumous honorary office, not an enfeoffment; by edict also restores 詔.
故河中節度使 is Hezhong, not Hedong (河東), and 諸子 marks Wang Zan as one among several sons.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故河中節度使重盈之諸子也

decisions.reason: The literal field likewise renders 河中 as Hedong; Hezhong is the command named in the Chinese.
既平河中 repeats the same command-name; pacified Hezhong, not Hedong.
The literal 平河中 must be Hezhong, matching the father's 河中節度使 in s0110.
檢校太傅 is already rendered as Grand Mentor in nearby units (s0029, s0172). Grand Tutor is only another English label for the same office, so the change is stylistic, not a source error.
贈太子太師 is a posthumous honorary office, not a fief.
The literal 贈 likewise is honorary bestowal, not enfeoffment.
甥 is the sister's son. 'Nephew by marriage' invents an affine tie; the preceding princess units identify the Founder's sister as the link.
The literal field repeats 'nephew by marriage' for 甥; sister's son is the kinship the Chinese marks.
蓚縣 is Tiao (a form of 蓨), not Zhuo (涿). The northern campaign context does not support reading 涿.
The literal field makes the same 蓚/涿 misreading; Tiao County matches 蓚縣.
s0172 already granted 檢校太傅 (Grand Mentor); 加檢校太尉 is a further advance to Taiwei, not another Grand Mentor of State.
The literal text conflates 太尉 with 太傅; acting grand commandant is the office added here.
累贈左僕射 is repeated posthumous honorary promotion. The idiomatic already has honored; the literal still wrongly says enfeoffed.
冊贈太師 is a patent granting a posthumous office; 追封 applies only to 楚國公. The original treats the first grant as an enfeoffment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 冊贈太師，周廣順中，贈中書令，追封楚國公

decisions.after: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of Grand Commandant.
decisions.reason: 詔贈太尉 is a posthumous honorary Taiwei, not an enfeoffment. The proposal keeps Grand Mentor of State, which is 太傅, so the office name remains wrong.
賜姓名 grants a surname and a given name together. 'Name Li' treats the imperial surname as the personal name and drops the given name conferred in that act.
不憫其親 does not mention torture, and 豈事文侯之宜 names Marquis Wen, not a generic worthy minister. The replacement restores both points without adding cruelty that the Chinese does not state here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 烏震不憫其親，仁斯鮮矣，雖慕樂羊之跡，豈事文侯之宜

claimRevisions.reason: The English office label followed the bad translation of 太尉 as Grand Mentor of State. The underlying posthumous grant remains; only the English name of 太尉 changes.
